questions.q: After the Contractor receives the Notice to Proceed (NTP), at what point does the contract time officially begin to be reckoned?
questions.n: Contract time begins to be reckoned on the 7th day following the receipt of the NTP.

questions.q: If a delay occurs, what is the allowed period for the Contractor to file a written request for a time extension?
questions.n: The Contractor must file the request within 15 days from the occurrence of the delay to be valid.

questions.q: How much advance notice is required from the Contractor before beginning, suspending, or resuming work operations?
questions.n: A 10-day notice allows the Architect and Owner enough time to prepare for inspection or administrative changes.

questions.q: What is the required lead time for a Contractor to request materials that are to be furnished by the Owner?
questions.n: The Owner requires a 10-day advance notice to coordinate the delivery of Owner-furnished materials.

questions.q: What is the minimum duration that must pass after a demand for drawings before the Contractor can file a claim for delay?
questions.n: The Architect is given a 2-week window to provide requested drawings before it constitutes a delay.

questions.q: After receiving the Notice to Proceed, what is the deadline for the Contractor to submit the Contract Sum Breakdown?
questions.n: The Contractor must submit the detailed breakdown within 15 days of receiving the NTP.

questions.q: If the Contractor receives instructions that they believe involve extra cost, within how many days must they notify the Architect?
questions.n: The Contractor must provide notice of extra cost within 15 days to protect their claim.

questions.q: What is the deadline for the Architect to act on (approve or deny) a Contractor’s payment request?
questions.n: The Architect has a 15-day window to evaluate and act upon the request for payment.

questions.q: Once the Architect has approved a payment request, how much time does the Owner have to act on or pay the request?
questions.n: The Owner must release payment within 15 days of the Architect's approval.

questions.q: What is the timeframe for the release of Retention money after the date of final payment?
questions.n: The remaining retention is typically released 3 months after final payment/acceptance.

questions.q: If the Owner removes 'condemned work' from the site, what is the deadline for the Contractor to pay the associated expenses?
questions.n: The Contractor has 10 days to reimburse the Owner for the costs of removing faulty work.

questions.q: If the Contractor fails to pay for the removal of condemned work, the Owner may sell the materials after giving how many days of notice?
questions.n: A 10-day notice must be given before the Owner proceeds to sell the materials to recover costs.

questions.q: How long is the Guarantee Period during which a Contractor must remedy defects due to faulty materials or workmanship?
questions.n: The standard Guarantee Period for construction work is one year from the date of final acceptance.

questions.q: Upon receiving written notice from the Owner, what is the deadline for the Contractor to perform repairs or corrective work?
questions.n: The Contractor is expected to start/perform corrective work within 5 days of notice.

questions.q: What is the time limit for a Sub-contractor to make a claim for extra cost to the Contractor?
questions.n: The claim must be made within one week from the incident or instruction causing the cost.

questions.q: If a Contractor intends to suspend work or terminate a contract, what is the specific notice period required?
questions.n: A 15-day written notice is required before the Contractor can legally suspend work or terminate.

questions.q: What is the minimum duration of a work stoppage ordered by a court (not due to Contractor's fault) that allows the Contractor to terminate the contract?
questions.n: If work is stopped for 90 days by court order through no fault of the Contractor, they may terminate.

questions.q: If an arbitrator awards a sum to the Contractor, how many days does the Owner have to pay before the Contractor can terminate the contract?
questions.n: The Owner has 30 days to pay the sum awarded by arbitrators.

questions.q: What is the notice period required for the Owner to terminate a contract or notify the Surety of such intent?
questions.n: The Owner must give 15 days of notice before terminating the contract.

questions.q: If the Architect fails to render a decision on a dispute within this period, either party may then demand arbitration:
questions.n: If the Architect remains silent for 15 days, the parties can move to arbitration.

questions.q: How many days of notice must an Insurance Company give the Owner before cancelling a Contractor’s Liability Insurance?
questions.n: Insurance companies must provide a 10-day warning before a policy is cancelled.

questions.q: Which bond remains in effect until it is replaced by the Guarantee Bond?
questions.n: These bonds cover the construction phase and are replaced by the guarantee bond upon completion.

questions.q: What is the effective period of the Guarantee Bond, starting from the date of final acceptance?
questions.n: The Guarantee Bond is valid for one year to cover any defects found after acceptance.

questions.q: If the Architect fails to act on payment requests within 15 days, what right does the Contractor have?
o: Double the amount of the bill
questions.n: Failure to act on payments is a fundamental breach that allows for work stoppage or termination.

questions.q: What is the basis of the 'Invitation' issued by the Client to prospective bidders, especially when prepared by another Architect?
questions.n: The invitation is for Competitive Bidding to ensure the Owner gets the best value and price.
